features: ⚠️ THIS VERSION ADDS NO DATABASE MIGRATIONS, but it fixes one that stopped halfway and left the database incomplete. If you already updated to 1.10.0 without trouble, there is nothing to redo.

THE UPDATE NO LONGER KEEPS THE OLD VERSION AROUND — After updating from the panel, the program could end up with the new code but the old list of pages: some new screens did not exist at all, and the tools you would use to find out why refused to start. The internal cache cleanup was deleting a hand-written list of files, and one of those names changed inside Laravel years ago. It now clears everything instead of trusting a list. ⚠️ Note: this fix applies to updates that start from the new version. The one you are running now still uses the updater from the version you are leaving, because the installed version is what provides it. If you ran «php artisan optimize» before updating, run «php artisan optimize:clear» straight afterwards; if you never did, there is nothing to do.

THE DATABASE NO LONGER STOPS HALFWAY — Updating from an earlier version with settings held in cache left the database update stuck on the first new setting, with ten steps still pending and no understandable message. That step now recognises an older configuration and carries on with the right value.

THE PROGRAM STARTS EVEN WHILE YOU ARE UPDATING IT — A manual update has a gap, as long as a download, where the code is already new and the libraries are still old. In that gap the program would not start at all, and the error named neither the cause nor the cure: even the commands you need to finish the update stopped working. That gap is now crossable.

DOCKER STARTUP: DEPENDENCIES ACTUALLY GET UPDATED — Anyone using Docker for development was left with the previous version's libraries and assets, because the check was «the folder exists» rather than «the folder is current». Dependencies are now installed on every start — when there is nothing to do it costs a few seconds — and pages are rebuilt when the code has changed.

AND THE SAME PROBLEM IN FOUR MORE PLACES — Reviewing this version we found the rows-per-page setting was being read without a safety net elsewhere too: one of those places sits on the path of every list in the program, so after an update with the old configuration still cached, no screen with a list would open at all — not one. The other three prevented opening and saving the general settings. All fixed, with an automatic check added so it cannot come back.

SECURITY: updated the library that renders formatted text, which had six open advisories — four high and two medium. Five were cases where specially crafted text could tie up the server far more than it should; the sixth was different: a way around the filter that blocks dangerous links.
